item.title: Housing Market Jitters Grip Australia Banks on Cautious Outlook
item.description: Banks revealed the extent of the depressed housing market sentiment in Australia this week, dragging down their share prices and underscoring the pressure on profitability.

item.title: China’s Coal-to-Chemicals Push Pays Off With Record Profits
item.description: China’s decade-plus quest to replace oil with coal in chemicals production is paying off for industry leader Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group Co., which pulled in record profits as crude prices soared due to the Middle East War.

item.title: Anthropic Said in Talks to Buy Startup Decart for $6 Billion
item.description: Anthropic PBC is in talks to buy the artificial intelligence startup Decart AI for about $6 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Australia Home Price Drop Adds to Restrictive Stance: RBA’s Kent
item.description: Australia’s softening housing market is contributing to financial conditions potentially being a bit more restrictive than otherwise, the Reserve Bank’s Assistant Governor Chris Kent said at an event.

item.title: Japan’s Producer Price Gains Stay High as BOJ Mulls Rate Path
item.description: Prices for Japan’s corporate goods continued to rise at an elevated pace in July, keeping high cost pressure on companies, as central bank officials continue to consider whether to proceed with additional interest rate hikes to contain inflation.

item.title: Brazil Backs Spending Control Measure in Fiscal Nod From Lula
item.description: Brazil’s Congress approved measures to curb spending growth in a move that aims to signal greater budget discipline backed by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ahead of his reelection bid later this year.

item.title: Korean Stocks Rise 23% in 10 Days as Chip Rally Regains Steam
item.description: South Korean stocks climbed, putting the benchmark index on track to enter a technical bull market, as a global rebound in the AI trade fueled a rapid reversal from last month’s historic rout.

item.title: A Trader’s Guide to Prabowo’s 2027 Indonesia State Budget Speech
item.description: Traders will be watching whether Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s state budget speech on Friday can convince investors that fiscal discipline remains a priority, helping restore confidence in the country’s battered assets.

item.title: Treasury Wine Earnings Drop by 36% on Global Alcohol Downturn
item.description: Treasury Wine Estates Ltd.’s full-year earnings fell by more than a third as the company battled a global downturn in alcohol consumption and supply concerns in China and the US.

item.title: Singapore Top Property Firms’ Profit Grows, Signal Recovery
item.description: Two of Singapore’s biggest property-focused firms reported improved first-half profit, helped by growing fee-related business and new project launches, as they seek to rebuild investor confidence after past setbacks.

item.title: ASX Profit Misses Estimates as Attia Prepares to Lead Exchange
item.description: ASX Ltd.’s full-year profit missed estimates and costs grew ahead of incoming chief executive officer Anthony Attia’s arrival at the Australian exchange next month.

item.title: Origin Profit Beats Estimates on Australian EV, Battery Uptake
item.description: Origin Energy Ltd.’s full-year profit beat analyst estimates, as the uptake of electric vehicles and home batteries in Australia accelerated.

item.title: Gold Steadies After Tame US Inflation Data Eases Rate-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold steadied near $4,400 an ounce after a subdued US inflation report relieved near-term pressure on the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates.

item.title: Surveyors Turn Most Downbeat on London House Prices Since 2023
item.description: Estate agents are more gloomy about London house prices than at any point in almost three years, according to a survey that suggests the property market malaise gripping the UK capital is deepening.

item.title: Asian Stocks Poised to Gain on Benign US Inflation: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia were poised for gains Thursday after the latest US inflation report matched expectations, easing concerns about imminent Federal Reserve rate increases.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 13
item.description: Oil edged lower after a five-session advance, as traders waited for signs of progress toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: EQT Offers $4.9 Billion to Buy Australia’s Cleanaway Waste
item.description: EQT Infrastructure offered to buy Cleanaway Waste Management Ltd. in a deal that values the Australian listed firm at about A$6.9 billion ($4.9 billion).

item.title: ANZ Profit Rises on Deposit Growth, Expansion in Business Loans
item.description: ANZ Group Holdings Ltd.’s profit climbed in the third quarter as the bank grew customer deposits and lending expanded in its business and private banking division.

item.title: Indonesian Tech Firm GoTo Cut From MSCI Indexes in Review
item.description: MSCI Inc. removed GoTo Group from its indexes after a plunge in the Indonesian tech company’s share price left the stock difficult to trade.

item.title: US Home Prices Keep Buyers Priced Out. Share Your Story
item.description: Home prices across the US continue to soar, fueling frustration for buyers and renters. Are you one of them? Our reporters want to hear your story.

item.title: Rio Tinto Aluminum Smelter Gets $1.8 Billion Australian Bailout
item.description: The owners of Australia’s biggest aluminum smelter, including Rio Tinto Group, have secured a government bailout of A$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion) to keep the plant operating as it grapples with high energy costs.

item.title: US Regulator Denies Egan-Jones Bid to Expand Ratings Business
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission rejected credit rating firm Egan-Jones Ratings Co.’s application to re-enter the market for grading government debt and asset-backed securities, the latest sign of regulatory pushback against the small but prolific agency.

item.title: Thousands of India Workers Are Helping AI Firms Train Robots to Replace Them
item.description: Robotics companies are competing to collect videos of humans stitching shoes and welding steel to give their machines new skills.

item.title: Fermi Names McIntire CEO Four Months After Ousting Co-Founder
item.description: Fermi Inc. has named Lee McIntire as chief executive officer, about four months after ousting its co-founder from the top job.

item.title: AI Cloud Provider Lambda Prices Loan for Nvidia-Tied Chip Deal
item.description: Lambda Inc., an AI cloud-computing provider backed by Nvidia Corp., wrapped up a $926 million leveraged-loan deal as that market becomes a new front in the borrowing binge to finance the artificial intelligence buildout.

item.title: CoreWeave Warns of Difficulty If It Must Shift From Nvidia Chips
item.description: CoreWeave Inc. is warning investors of the time and money it may take to shift from its exclusive use of Nvidia Corp. artificial intelligence chips.

item.title: Apple App Store Rate Proceeding Halted by Supreme Court for Now
item.description: Apple Inc. won a one-day reprieve from the Supreme Court Wednesday as Justice Elena Kagan paused proceedings before a California trial court in the iPhone maker’s long-running antitrust feud with Fortnite-maker Epic Games Inc.

item.title: Cisco’s Sales Top Estimates, But Fail to Live Up to the Hype
item.description: Cisco Systems Inc. delivered quarterly revenue and profit that beat estimates, but failed to live up to investors’ high expectations following blow-out results in the previous period.

item.title: Cerebras Shares Tumble After Sales Decline at Hardware Business
item.description: Cerebras Systems Inc. slid in late trading after reporting a decline in hardware revenue, a sign the newly public company is making slow progress selling computers with a novel chip design.

item.title: Two Sigma’s Overdeck Offered Wife $633 Million, Her Lawyer Says
item.description: Two Sigma Investments’ billionaire co-founder John Overdeck schemed to leave his wife Laura “with as little as possible,” her lawyer said as the couple’s divorce trial began, an amount she pegged at $633 million.
